To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a): females were significantly more likely to perceive constraints on their participation in recreational sport than males, especially time-related and intrapersonal ones; (b): less-educated individuals were significantly more likely than better-educated ones to perceive constraints on recreational sport; (c): age was significantly associated with the perception of constraints; the perception of constraints was higher among younger (18-29 years) and older (50+ years) individuals than those in the middle age group (30-49 years),
there are significant differences in the perception and the experience of leisure constraint among demographic groups.
the perception of leisure constraints on sport participation varies according to demographic characteristics.

the following questions.
the relationship between sport participation and the perception of leisure constraints.

the following question: Are any sub-groups (i.e. females, less-educated individuals, married individuals, older individuals) of the Greek population, particularly influenced by the perception of constraints in their recreational sport participation?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is a significant difference in the perception of leisure constraints on recreational sport between the various sub-groups of the population, and this difference may be related to the annual sport-participation rate of each group.
the results of this study are consistent with the propositions of the leisure constraint model and the negotiation and balance theories.
the results of this research study are consistent with those of previous studies.

demographic differences in the perception and experience of leisure constraints are important and should be taken into account when developing sport and leisure policies.
